Routing observations:
- Option C was rejected for 9 of 10 tickets, with the system explicitly stating “option C is not valid.”
- The sole successful C selection was REQ-2408: a small shipment from the north region, submitted by Regional Ops after a bounced first attempt. Its C label appeared as “regional…”/“regional office.”
- Do not select C by default; it may only be valid for a narrow regional-office case, possibly north-region shipments handled by Regional Ops.
- No evidence yet distinguishes when to choose A (standard queue) versus B (priority desk). Ticket size, request type, region, sender, and urgency wording may affect this, but the failed examples cannot establish the rule because C was selected every time.
- For future tickets, inspect the complete option labels and prefer A or B unless the request clearly matches the validated regional-office pattern.

Routing observations:
- Option C was previously rejected 9/10 times, but that pattern is no longer reliable. Recent tickets show A and B explicitly rejected across varied regions, sizes, and request types.
- Confirmed successful choice: REQ-2408, small north-region shipment from Regional Ops after a bounced first attempt, with C labeled “regional…”.
- REQ-2410: A was accepted for a small east-region claim from Regional Ops, showing that regional-office origin does not automatically require C.
- A was rejected for REQ-2411 (large north invoice), REQ-2412 (large north shipment, second attempt), REQ-2416 (large south shipment), REQ-2417 (small east shipment), REQ-2418 (small south claim), and REQ-2419 (small south shipment).
- B was rejected for REQ-2413–2415 (large east claims/invoice), including requests mentioning the regional office or repeated follow-up.
- The current evidence strongly suggests C (or another newly displayed option such as D) may be required for many tickets, but the rule is not yet identified. Do not assume A is the safe default.
- Inspect complete, uncropped option labels, including any D option, and account for request type, region, size, sender, wording, prior attempts, and the shipment procedure change.
- Treat each accepted/rejected result as evidence; avoid generalizing from the older C-heavy failures.

Routing observations:
- Do not use A as a safe default or assume Regional Ops requires C. Older C-heavy rejection patterns are unreliable.
- Inspect complete, uncropped labels, including D. Track request type, region, size, sender, wording, urgency, prior attempts, and the shipment-procedure change.
- Confirmed acceptances:
  - REQ-2408: C; small north shipment, Regional Ops, bounced first attempt, “regional…” label.
  - REQ-2410: A; small east claim, Regional Ops.
  - REQ-2423: D; small east invoice, Partner Accounts, “anything missing.”
  - REQ-2425: D; large north shipment, Finance Desk, end-of-day urgency.
  - REQ-2429: D; large north claim, Partner Accounts, scanned paperwork.
- Recent C rejections:
  - REQ-2420: small north claim, Regional Ops, receipt confirmation.
  - REQ-2424: large north refund, Field Sales.
  - REQ-2427: small east invoice, Regional Ops, repeated follow-up.
  - REQ-2428: small east shipment, Regional Ops, second attempt.
  These reinforce that region, origin, and prior attempts alone do not determine C.
- Recent D rejections:
  - REQ-2421: small east refund, Regional Ops, scanned paperwork.
  - REQ-2422 and REQ-2426: large south claims with similar “last month” wording, from Field Sales and Partner Accounts.
  Thus D is not universally correct; acceptance may depend on combinations of type, region, size, sender, wording, or procedure timing.
- A was rejected for REQ-2411, 2412, 2416–2419; B was rejected for REQ-2413–2415.
- Treat every outcome as evidence. The claim-procedure change may matter, but its effective boundary and rule remain unidentified.

Routing observations:
- Do not use A as a safe default, assume Regional Ops requires C, or assume scanned paperwork requires D. No single region, sender, size, type, wording, or urgency reliably determines the option.
- Inspect complete, uncropped labels, including D. Track request type, region, size, sender, wording, urgency, prior attempts, and procedure timing/change.
- Confirmed acceptances:
  - REQ-2408: C; small north shipment, Regional Ops, bounced first attempt, “regional…”
  - REQ-2410: A; small east claim, Regional Ops.
  - REQ-2423: D; small east invoice, Partner Accounts, “anything missing.”
  - REQ-2425: D; large north shipment, Finance Desk, end-of-day urgency.
  - REQ-2429: D; large north claim, Partner Accounts, scanned paperwork.
  - REQ-2432: D; large north claim, Finance Desk, scanned paperwork.
  - REQ-2433: A; small south claim, Regional Ops, scanned paperwork.
  - REQ-2438: A; small south invoice, Regional Ops, “same as last month.”
- New rejections:
  - D failed for REQ-2430 (large north invoice, Field Sales, receipt confirmation), REQ-2431 (small east shipment, Partner Accounts, end-of-day), REQ-2435 (large south invoice, Finance Desk, receipt confirmation), REQ-2436 (small north refund, Partner Accounts), REQ-2437 (large east invoice, Field Sales, “anything missing”), and REQ-2439 (small south claim, Regional Ops, scanned paperwork).
  - A failed for REQ-2434 (small north invoice, Client Services, regional-office wording).
- Invoice procedure change is relevant but its effective boundary/rule remains unidentified; do not generalize from the memo alone.
- Treat every outcome as evidence; preserve contradictory examples rather than forcing a simple rule.

Routing observations:
- No single region, sender/desk, size, request type, wording, urgency, scanned status, or label option is a reliable rule. Do not use A as default, assume Regional Ops means C, or assume scanned paperwork means D.
- Inspect complete, uncropped labels, including D. Track all fields, prior attempts, and procedure timing/changes. Preserve contradictions.
- Confirmed acceptances:
  - C: REQ-2408.
  - A: REQ-2410, REQ-2433, REQ-2438.
  - D: REQ-2423, REQ-2425, REQ-2429, REQ-2432, REQ-2444.
  - B: REQ-2445, REQ-2446.
- Recent rejections:
  - D: REQ-2430, REQ-2431, REQ-2435, REQ-2436, REQ-2437, REQ-2439, REQ-2440, REQ-2448.
  - A: REQ-2434, REQ-2442.
  - C: REQ-2441, REQ-2447.
  - B: REQ-2443, REQ-2449.
- The same/similar attributes can map to different options: east small shipment/end-of-day was B (REQ-2446) but D failed (REQ-2431); east large shipment/regional-office was C-failed (REQ-2441); south scanned claims were B-accepted (large, REQ-2445) and D-rejected (small, REQ-2439).
- Invoice procedure change is relevant, but its effective boundary/rule remains unidentified; do not generalize from the memo alone. A claim procedure change also takes effect soon—record timing and reassess claims near the boundary.

Routing observations:
- No single region, sender/desk, size, request type, wording, urgency, scanned status, or label option is a reliable rule. Do not default to A, assume Regional Ops means C, or assume scanned paperwork means D.
- Inspect complete, uncropped labels, including D. Track every field, prior attempts, and procedure timing/changes; preserve contradictions.
- Confirmed acceptances:
  - C: REQ-2408.
  - A: REQ-2410, REQ-2433, REQ-2438.
  - D: REQ-2423, REQ-2425, REQ-2429, REQ-2432, REQ-2444.
  - B: REQ-2445, REQ-2446, REQ-2452 (south, small claim, scanned), REQ-2456 (east, small refund, end-of-day), REQ-2459 (south, large claim, Regional Ops wording).
- Recent rejections:
  - D: REQ-2430, REQ-2431, REQ-2435, REQ-2436, REQ-2437, REQ-2439, REQ-2440, REQ-2448.
  - A: REQ-2434, REQ-2442, REQ-2457 (east, large invoice).
  - C: REQ-2441, REQ-2447.
  - B: REQ-2443, REQ-2449, REQ-2450 (east, large claim), REQ-2451 (east, large refund), REQ-2453 (north, large claim), REQ-2454 (north, small refund, scanned), REQ-2455 (east, large claim), REQ-2458 (north, large shipment, second attempt).
- Similar attributes still diverge: south scanned claims include B-accepted large (REQ-2445), B-accepted small (REQ-2452), and D-rejected small (REQ-2439); east large claims rejected under B (REQ-2450/2455), while south large Regional Ops claim was B-accepted.
- Refund procedure change takes effect soon; invoice change is relevant but its boundary/rule remains unknown. A claim procedure change also takes effect soon. Record timing and reassess requests near boundaries.
